name: Elena Biagi

primary_works.title: Through ageing, and beyond: gut microbiota and inflammatory status in seniors and centenarians (PLoS ONE)

field_contribution: Characterized the remodeling of the gut microbiota across aging into the centenarian range and linked compositional shifts to inflammatory status, connecting the microbiome to the inflammaging framework.
why_indexed: An early, much-cited demonstration that the aging gut microbiome tracks systemic inflammation.

name: Claudio Franceschi

primary_works.title: Inflamm-aging: an evolutionary perspective on immunosenescence (Annals NY Acad Sci)
Inflammaging and Garb-aging (Trends in Endocrinology & Metabolism)

field_contribution: Coined 'inflammaging', the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that accompanies aging, and the related 'garb-aging' (accumulated molecular debris) concept, and built centenarian-biology cohorts to test them.
why_indexed: Inflammaging is one of the organizing concepts of mechanistic geroscience; indexed at the framework level.

name: Fedor Galkin
region: Insilico Medicine / Deep Longevity, Hong Kong

primary_works.title: Human gut microbiome aging clock based on taxonomic profiling and deep learning (iScience)
Deep biomarkers of aging and longevity (blood/psychological clocks)

field_contribution: Built deep-learning aging clocks across modalities (blood biochemistry, microbiome, psychological/behavioral data), productizing biological-age estimation at a commercial longevity company.
why_indexed: Indexed as a principal builder of commercial multimodal AI aging clocks; the productization edge of the clock field.
disputed: Commercial deep-learning clocks have weaker independent validation and reproducibility documentation than academic clocks; vendor COI.

name: William E. Kraus

primary_works.title: 2 years of calorie restriction and cardiometabolic risk: CALERIE (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology)
STRRIDE exercise-dose trials

field_contribution: Principal investigator of CALERIE, the only long-term randomized controlled trial of sustained caloric restriction in non-obese humans, which showed cardiometabolic improvements without harm, and led the STRRIDE exercise-dose-response trials.
why_indexed: CALERIE is the anchor of human caloric-restriction evidence; every CR-in-humans claim routes through it.

name: Krista A. Varady

primary_works.title: Effects of alternate-day fasting vs daily calorie restriction: Trepanowski et al. (JAMA Internal Medicine)
Cardiometabolic benefits of intermittent fasting (Annual Review of Nutrition)

field_contribution: A leading intermittent-fasting and alternate-day-fasting researcher whose own randomized trial found ADF produced no greater weight loss or cardiometabolic benefit than daily caloric restriction, a credible null from inside the fasting field.
why_indexed: The rigorous within-field counterweight to over-claimed intermittent-fasting benefits.

name: Stephen J. Simpson
region: University of Sydney (Charles Perkins Centre), Australia

primary_works.title: The Geometric Framework for nutrition
The ratio of macronutrients, not caloric intake, dictates lifespan: Solon-Biet et al. (Cell Metabolism)

field_contribution: Co-architect of the Geometric Framework of Nutrition, which models how animals balance multiple nutrients, and co-led the mouse work showing lifespan is governed by the protein:carbohydrate ratio rather than total calories.
why_indexed: Reframed the diet-longevity question from 'how many calories' to 'what macronutrient balance', a foundational shift.

name: David G. Le Couteur

primary_works.title: The ratio of macronutrients, not caloric intake, dictates lifespan: Solon-Biet et al. (Cell Metabolism)
Macronutrients, FGF21, and nutrient sensing in aging

field_contribution: Co-led the macronutrient-ratio mouse-lifespan program and connected it to nutrient-sensing biology (mTOR, FGF21), bridging the nutrition-geometry findings to the molecular hallmarks of aging.
why_indexed: Links the macronutrient-balance result to mechanistic nutrient-sensing, the bridge between Domain D and the aging hallmarks.

name: Samantha M. Solon-Biet

primary_works.title: The ratio of macronutrients dictates cardiometabolic health, aging, and longevity (Cell Metabolism)
Branched-chain amino acids impact health and lifespan (Nature Metabolism)

field_contribution: First author of the definitive protein-ratio mouse-longevity experiment showing low-protein/high-carbohydrate diets maximized lifespan, and later work isolating branched-chain amino acids as drivers of the protein effect.
why_indexed: The strongest controlled experimental support for protein restriction extending lifespan; a load-bearing node in the protein/mTOR conflict.

name: Jaime Guevara-Aguirre
region: Universidad San Francisco de Quito, Ecuador

primary_works.title: Growth hormone receptor deficiency reduces pro-aging signaling, cancer, and diabetes: Guevara-Aguirre & Longo (Science Translational Medicine)

field_contribution: Followed an Ecuadorian cohort with Laron syndrome (growth-hormone-receptor deficiency, very low IGF-1) for decades, documenting near-absence of cancer and diabetes despite obesity, the human natural experiment in the IGF-1/protein-longevity debate.
why_indexed: The principal human evidence that low GH/IGF-1 signaling protects against age-related disease.

name: Jurgen M. Bauer

primary_works.title: Evidence-based recommendations for optimal dietary protein intake in older people: PROT-AGE study group (JAMDA)

field_contribution: Led the PROT-AGE consensus recommending higher protein intake (>=1.0-1.2 g/kg/day) for older adults to preserve muscle and function, the elderly-protein evidence base that runs against blanket low-protein-for-longevity prescriptions.
why_indexed: The clinical anchor of the 'older adults need MORE protein' position in the protein conflict.

name: Dariush Mozaffarian

primary_works.title: Effects on coronary heart disease of increasing polyunsaturated fat in place of saturated fat: a meta-analysis of RCTs (PLoS Medicine)

field_contribution: Cardiovascular nutrition epidemiologist whose meta-analysis of randomized trials found that replacing saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat lowers coronary events, the mainstream evidentiary counter to the 'seed oils are toxic' claim.
why_indexed: The reference rebuttal in the seed-oil/PUFA nutrition conflict.

name: Christopher E. Ramsden

primary_works.title: Re-evaluation of the traditional diet-heart hypothesis: Minnesota Coronary Experiment (BMJ)
Use of dietary linoleic acid for secondary prevention: Sydney Diet Heart Study (BMJ)

field_contribution: Recovered and re-analyzed lost raw data from old randomized diet-heart trials (Minnesota Coronary Experiment, Sydney Diet Heart), finding that lowering saturated fat by raising linoleic acid did not reduce, and may have increased, mortality.
why_indexed: The most-cited empirical data on the linoleic-acid-skeptic side of the seed-oil debate.

name: James J. DiNicolantonio
region: Saint Luke's Mid America Heart Institute, USA

primary_works.title: Omega-6 vegetable oils as a driver of coronary heart disease: the oxidized linoleic acid hypothesis: DiNicolantonio & O'Keefe (Open Heart)
The Salt Fix

field_contribution: A principal popularizer of the hypothesis that omega-6 'seed oils' and their oxidized linoleic-acid metabolites (OXLAMs) drive coronary disease, and of contrarian salt and saturated-fat positions.
why_indexed: The most visible node of the seed-oils-cause-disease narrative; indexed at hypothesis tier (mechanism marketed as established outcome). INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: Presents a mechanistic hypothesis (OXLAM to CHD) as settled; the outcome claim is not supported by RCT evidence (cf. Mozaffarian).

name: James H. O'Keefe
region: Saint Luke's Mid America Heart Institute, USA

primary_works.title: Omega-6 vegetable oils as a driver of coronary heart disease (Open Heart)
Potential adverse cardiovascular effects from excessive endurance exercise (Mayo Clinic Proceedings)

field_contribution: Preventive cardiologist and co-author of the oxidized-linoleic-acid CHD hypothesis; also a proponent of the 'too much endurance exercise harms the heart' (cardiac-overuse) position.
why_indexed: Co-author node on the seed-oils-skeptic side and the endurance-overdose debate. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: Shares the OXLAM hypothesis's outcome-overstatement problem; the excessive-endurance-harm claim is contested.

name: Ramon Estruch
region: University of Barcelona / Hospital Clinic, Spain

primary_works.title: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease with a Mediterranean diet: PREDIMED (NEJM, retracted & republished)

field_contribution: Led PREDIMED, the largest randomized trial of the Mediterranean diet for cardiovascular prevention, which reported reduced major cardiovascular events. The trial was retracted and republished in 2018 after randomization irregularities were found and corrected.
why_indexed: PREDIMED is the strongest Mediterranean-diet outcome RCT; its retraction/republication is a trial-integrity case study indexed for both reasons.
disputed: 2018 retraction/republication after discovery that part of the cohort was not individually randomized; corrected analysis upheld the main finding.

name: Saul Justin Newman
region: University College London / Oxford (formerly ANU), UK/Australia

primary_works.title: Supercentenarians and the oldest-old are concentrated into regions with no birth certificates and short lifespans (bioRxiv)
Ig Nobel Prize (Demography)

field_contribution: Demographer whose data-quality analyses argue that supercentenarian and Blue-Zone longevity records concentrate in places with poor birth registration, high poverty, and pension-fraud incentives, implying many extreme-age records are clerical error or fraud.
why_indexed: The key skeptic of Blue Zones and extreme-longevity claims; indexed as the falsification pressure on the longevity-hotspot narrative.
disputed: Findings remain a working-paper/contested critique; defenders dispute the fraud framing for validated cohorts.

name: John C. Newman
region: Buck Institute for Research on Aging / UCSF, USA

primary_works.title: Ketone bodies as signaling metabolites: Newman & Verdin (Annual Review of Nutrition)
Ketogenic diet reduces midlife mortality and improves memory in aging mice (Cell Metabolism)

field_contribution: Buck Institute geroscientist studying beta-hydroxybutyrate as a signaling molecule (HDAC inhibition, inflammasome suppression) and the healthspan effects of ketogenic diets in aging mice. Distinct from the demographer Saul Justin Newman.
why_indexed: Grounds ketone/ketogenic-diet longevity claims in mechanism (BHB signaling) and controlled mouse experiments.
cross_branch_note: Distinct person from Saul Justin Newman (demographer)

name: Michael J. Joyner

primary_works.title: Modeling: optimal marathon performance on the basis of physiological factors (J. Applied Physiology)
Endurance exercise performance: the physiology of champions (J. Physiology, with Coyle)

field_contribution: Defined the physiological model of human endurance performance, the interaction of VO2max, lactate threshold, and running economy that sets the ceiling on aerobic capacity, and the prediction of sub-2-hour marathon feasibility.
why_indexed: The reference framework for what limits human aerobic performance; Attia's cited exercise physiologist on VO2max as a longevity predictor.

name: Bruce Ames
region: UC Berkeley / Children's Hospital Oakland Research Institute, USA

primary_works.title: Low micronutrient intake may accelerate degenerative diseases of aging through triage allocation (PNAS)
The Ames test for mutagenicity (PNAS)

field_contribution: Proposed the 'triage theory', that under micronutrient scarcity the body allocates vitamins/minerals to immediate survival at the expense of long-term maintenance, accelerating age-related disease, and earlier the mitochondrial-decay theory of aging and the Ames mutagenicity test.
why_indexed: Connects nutrition to mitochondria to aging via a falsifiable allocation principle; indexed for the triage/mitochondrial-decay framework.

name: Donald K. (Don) Layman

primary_works.title: A reduced ratio of dietary carbohydrate to protein improves body composition (J. Nutrition)
Defining meal requirements for protein to optimize metabolic roles of amino acids (Am J Clin Nutr)

field_contribution: Established the leucine 'threshold' and per-meal protein-distribution science, that muscle protein synthesis requires a per-meal leucine dose, shaping recommendations for protein quantity and timing.
why_indexed: The mechanistic basis under modern protein-per-meal and leucine-threshold recommendations.

name: Dan Garner
region: Rapid Health Optimization (with Andy Galpin), USA

primary_works.title: Rapid Health Optimization protocol (blood + biomarker performance profiling)

field_contribution: Andy Galpin's lab partner; builds comprehensive blood, hormone, and biomarker performance-profiling protocols for athletes and high performers, translating panels into individualized training/nutrition adjustments.
why_indexed: Indexed as a practitioner node for deep-biomarker performance optimization; N=1/applied tier, not primary research. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: William S. Harris
region: University of South Dakota / OmegaQuant, USA

primary_works.title: The Omega-3 Index: a new risk factor for death from coronary heart disease? (with von Schacky, Preventive Medicine)

field_contribution: Created the Omega-3 Index, the percentage of EPA+DHA in red-blood-cell membranes, establishing a standardized individual omega-3 status biomarker that links tissue fatty-acid composition to cardiovascular and mortality risk.
why_indexed: The biomarker beneath fish-oil/omega-3 longevity claims; indexed for the measurement, with vendor caveat.
disputed: Founder of OmegaQuant, which sells the Omega-3 Index test (commercial COI).

name: Jill Miller
region: Tune Up Fitness / Yoga Tune Up, USA

primary_works.title: The Roll Model
Yoga Tune Up / Tune Up Fitness method

field_contribution: Developed a self-myofascial-release and 'embodied anatomy' methodology integrating fascia work, breath, and mobility into corrective-exercise practice.
why_indexed: A widely-used applied fascia/self-massage system; indexed practitioner-tier (movement library), not primary science. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Brian Mackenzie

primary_works.title: Power Speed Endurance
Unbreakable Runner

field_contribution: Performance coach who systematized breathing protocols for athletic performance, stress resilience, and recovery, bridging breathwork with endurance training and cold exposure.
why_indexed: An applied node connecting breath to exercise to cold; practitioner/protocol tier. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Ori Hofmekler

primary_works.title: The Warrior Diet

field_contribution: Author of 'The Warrior Diet,' an early popular undereating/one-large-evening-meal protocol that anticipated modern intermittent fasting and time-restricted eating.
why_indexed: Indexed as a popular antecedent of intermittent fasting; protocol/practitioner tier, not research. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Glen Jeffery
region: University College London (Institute of Ophthalmology), UK

primary_works.title: Optically improved mitochondrial function redeems aged human visual decline (J. Gerontology)
670 nm red light improves aged retinal mitochondrial function

field_contribution: Showed that near-infrared/red light (~670 nm) improves mitochondrial function in aged retinal and systemic tissue, providing a controlled academic basis for photobiomodulation effects on cytochrome-c-oxidase and ATP.
why_indexed: The academic anchor under red-light/near-infrared mitochondrial claims; the credentialed end of a heavily marketed area.

name: Alexis Cowan

primary_works.title: PhD research on metabolic regulation (Princeton)
Light x metabolism public lectures and writing

field_contribution: Princeton-trained metabolism PhD who communicates the intersection of light exposure, circadian biology, and metabolic regulation to general audiences, serving as a credentialed translator of Kruse-adjacent light-metabolism ideas.
why_indexed: Indexed as a credentialed communicator bridging mainstream metabolism and light-biology heterodoxy. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: Communicator role; specific light-metabolism causal claims for humans remain under-evidenced.

name: T. Que Collins
region: Center for Deuterium Depletion / Cignature Health, USA

primary_works.title: Ketogenic diet and deuterium-depleted water for prevention and treatment of cancer (review)
Deuterium-depletion measurement technologies (patents)

field_contribution: Co-founder and principal investigator of the Center for Deuterium Depletion, advancing the hypothesis that lowering body deuterium (via deuterium-depleted water, ketogenic diets, and fatty-acid oxidation generating low-deuterium metabolic water) improves mitochondrial function and cancer/metabolic outcomes.
why_indexed: A central clinical/translational node of the deuterium-depletion program feeding the corpus's deuterium thread. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Richard J. Roberts (deuterium research)

primary_works.title: Summiting Everest in deuterium-depleting nutritional ketosis (case work, co-author)
Natural mechanisms of deuterium depletion and metabolic-water recycling

field_contribution: Researcher in the deuterium-depletion / metabolic-water circle (Collins/Boros milieu) studying how fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial metabolic water naturally deplete body deuterium, and applying it to ketosis and performance.
why_indexed: Indexed for the natural-deuterium-depletion mechanism within the corpus's deuterium thread. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: NOT the Nobel laureate Sir Richard J. Roberts (restriction enzymes/introns); documentation thin; deuterium-depletion outcome claims unproven.

name: Karl J. Friston
region: University College London (Queen Square Institute of Neurology), UK

primary_works.title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory? (Nature Reviews Neuroscience)
Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM)

field_contribution: Formulated the free-energy principle and active inference, the theory that self-organizing systems (brains) act to minimize variational free energy (prediction error), and earlier built Statistical Parametric Mapping, the standard framework for analyzing functional neuroimaging.
why_indexed: The leading mathematical theory of brain/mind organization; canon-tier for the mind branch, surfaced in this corpus via the mind/neuro thread.
cross_branch_note: primarily bucket-canon 07-mind (and 04-information); indexed here as a cross-branch figure

name: Donald D. Hoffman

primary_works.title: The Case Against Reality: Why Evolution Hid the Truth from Our Eyes
Objects of consciousness (Frontiers in Psychology)

field_contribution: Argues the interface theory of perception, that perception is a species-specific 'user interface' shaped by fitness rather than a veridical window onto reality, and a formal conscious-agent/conscious-realism model in which consciousness is fundamental.
why_indexed: A prominent contested theory of perception and consciousness; indexed for the mind branch, not endorsed.
cross_branch_note: primarily bucket-canon 07-mind; cross-branch figure indexed here
disputed: Conscious-realism is a minority, contested metaphysical position; the evolutionary-game arguments are debated.

name: Nolan Williams

primary_works.title: Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (SAINT/SNT) accelerated TMS for depression (American J. Psychiatry)
Psilocybin and neuromodulation clinical trials

field_contribution: Developed SAINT/SNT, an accelerated, individualized intermittent theta-burst transcranial magnetic stimulation protocol for treatment-resistant depression (FDA-cleared 2022), and runs psychedelic and neuromodulation trials.
why_indexed: A clinical-translation node for rapid neuromodulation; indexed via the corpus's recovery/mind thread.

name: Paul Conti

primary_works.title: Trauma: The Invisible Epidemic

field_contribution: Psychiatrist who frames trauma, drive, and agency as central to mental health, popularizing a clinical model of how chronic stress and trauma shape behavior and physiology, the stress-to-mind bridge in the corpus.
why_indexed: Indexed as a clinical communicator linking stress/trauma to the mind and recovery domains. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Dave Asprey

primary_works.title: The Bulletproof Diet
Game Changers

field_contribution: Originated the modern consumer 'biohacking' brand (Bulletproof Coffee, Bulletproof Diet) and popularized N=1 self-experimentation, mitochondrial-optimization framing, and deuterium-depletion to mass audiences.
why_indexed: The originating popular node of the biohacking subculture that distributes many corpus concepts; protocol/marketing tier. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.

name: Ben Greenfield

primary_works.title: Beyond Training
Boundless

field_contribution: Endurance athlete and biohacking communicator who synthesizes deuterium-depletion, structured-water, supplement, and N=1 protocols across a large podcast/audience.
why_indexed: An aggregator/distributor node for many corpus protocols; practitioner/marketing tier. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: Synthesizes contested protocols as advice; commercial COI; claims frequently outrun evidence.

name: Jeffrey J. Iliff
region: University of Washington / VA Puget Sound, USA

primary_works.title: A paravascular pathway facilitates CSF flow through the brain parenchyma and the clearance of interstitial solutes, including amyloid-beta (Science Translational Medicine)

field_contribution: Co-discovered the glymphatic system, the AQP4-dependent paravascular pathway by which cerebrospinal fluid clears interstitial waste (including amyloid-beta) from the brain, with clearance enhanced during sleep.
why_indexed: Co-author of the mechanistic basis of 'why sleep clears the brain'; foundational to sleep-neurodegeneration links.

name: Till Roenneberg

primary_works.title: Social jetlag and obesity / Munich ChronoType Questionnaire (Current Biology; Chronobiology International)
Internal Time: Chronotypes, Social Jet Lag, and Why You're So Tired

field_contribution: Coined 'social jetlag' (the mismatch between biological and social clocks) and operationalized human chronotype via the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire, turning circadian misalignment into a measurable population variable.
why_indexed: Created the standard human constructs, chronotype and social jetlag, for studying circadian misalignment and health.

name: Eve Van Cauter

primary_works.title: Impact of sleep debt on metabolic and endocrine function: Spiegel, Leproult & Van Cauter (The Lancet)

field_contribution: Ran the foundational human sleep-restriction experiments showing that curtailed sleep impairs glucose tolerance, raises evening cortisol, and disrupts appetite hormones, establishing the causal sleep-to-metabolic-dysfunction link.
why_indexed: The origin of experimental evidence that sleep loss directly damages metabolic and endocrine function.

name: George C. Brainard

primary_works.title: Action spectrum for melatonin regulation in humans: evidence for a novel circadian photoreceptor (J. Neuroscience)

field_contribution: Determined the human melatonin action spectrum, showing peak circadian sensitivity to short-wavelength (~460-480 nm blue) light, direct evidence for a non-rod/non-cone (melanopsin/ipRGC) circadian photoreceptor.
why_indexed: The empirical basis for blue-light circadian effects and melanopsin photoreception in humans.

name: Charles A. Czeisler
region: Harvard Medical School / Brigham and Women's Hospital, USA

primary_works.title: Bright light resets the human circadian pacemaker independent of the timing of the sleep-wake cycle (Science)
Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep: Chang et al. (PNAS)

field_contribution: Established human circadian photoreception and light-resetting of the master clock, including dose-response of light on phase, and was senior author on the demonstration that evening screen light suppresses melatonin and delays the clock.
why_indexed: Defined how light entrains the human circadian system, the physiology behind light-hygiene and shift-work guidance.

name: Bruce S. McEwen

primary_works.title: Stress and the individual: mechanisms leading to disease: McEwen & Stellar (Archives of Internal Medicine)
Protective and damaging effects of stress mediators (NEJM)

field_contribution: Introduced 'allostatic load', the cumulative physiological wear from chronic stress and repeated activation of stress-response systems, and mapped how stress hormones remodel the brain and body, providing the framework linking chronic stress to disease.
why_indexed: Allostatic load is the organizing concept for chronic-stress damage and recovery science.

name: Fred Shaffer

primary_works.title: An overview of heart rate variability metrics and norms (Frontiers in Public Health)
A healthy heart is not a metronome: HRV metrics and norms (Frontiers in Psychology)

field_contribution: Authored the standard reference reviews defining heart-rate-variability metrics (time-domain, frequency-domain, nonlinear) and their normative values, grounding HRV as an autonomic-recovery biomarker.
why_indexed: The reference grounding for HRV as a measurement, the methodological backbone of recovery/readiness tracking.

name: Joshua J. Gooley

primary_works.title: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans (J. Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism)

field_contribution: Quantified how ordinary indoor room light before bed suppresses melatonin and shortens its nightly duration in humans, extending circadian photoreception findings to everyday light environments.
why_indexed: Provided the real-world dose evidence that household lighting disrupts the circadian melatonin signal.

name: Alexei Guzey

primary_works.title: Matthew Walker's 'Why We Sleep' Is Riddled with Scientific and Factual Errors (essay)

field_contribution: Wrote the widely-cited documented critique of Matthew Walker's 'Why We Sleep,' cataloguing factual and citation errors, and founded New Science (a meta-science reform organization).
why_indexed: Indexed as critique-tier provenance for the Walker sleep-claims conflict, the documented skeptic counterweight. INCLUSION does not equal ENDORSEMENT.
disputed: The critique is a non-peer-reviewed web essay; some points are contested and Walker has partially rebutted.

name: Allan D. Sniderman
region: McGill University (Mike Rosenbloom Laboratory for Cardiovascular Research), Montreal, Canada

primary_works.title: Apolipoproteins versus lipids as indices of coronary risk and as targets for statin therapy (Lancet)
A meta-analysis of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and apoB as markers of cardiovascular risk (Circ Cardiovasc Qual Outcomes)

field_contribution: Argued that apolipoprotein B (apoB) - a count of atherogenic particle number, one apoB per LDL/VLDL/IDL/Lp(a) particle - is a more accurate index of cardiovascular risk than LDL-cholesterol concentration, and defined the 'discordance' framework in which apoB and LDL-C diverge and apoB tracks outcomes better.
why_indexed: The principal architect of the case that particle number, not cholesterol mass, is the causal lipid exposure to measure - the conceptual root of the apoB-over-LDL-C debate.
disputed: His position that apoB should replace LDL-C as the primary clinical target is accepted in principle but only partially adopted in guidelines, which still lead with LDL-C for cost/availability reasons.

name: Brian A. Ference
region: University of Cambridge, UK (also University of Milan)

primary_works.title: Low-density lipoproteins cause atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease - EAS Consensus Panel (Eur Heart J)
Mendelian randomization studies of LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular events (multivariable MR)

field_contribution: Used Mendelian randomization - naturally randomized lifelong genetic exposure to lower LDL/apoB - to triangulate genetic, epidemiological, and randomized-trial evidence into the claim that LDL/apoB is causal for atherosclerosis and that risk depends on cumulative exposure (LDL x time), not just current level.
why_indexed: Lead author of the consensus that reframed LDL/apoB from 'risk marker' to 'causal cumulative exposure', the strongest formal synthesis of the lipid-causality argument.
cross_branch_note: links to causal-inference (Mendelian randomization) method shared with genetics branch
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (LDL-causal EAS consensus + multivariable MR)

name: Pia R. Kamstrup

primary_works.title: Genetically elevated lipoprotein(a) and increased risk of myocardial infarction (JAMA)
Extreme lipoprotein(a) levels and risk of myocardial infarction in the general population (Circulation)

field_contribution: Provided Mendelian-randomization evidence from the Copenhagen general-population cohorts that lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], an LDL-like particle whose level is ~90% genetically determined by the LPA gene, is a causal - not merely correlated - risk factor for myocardial infarction.
why_indexed: The genetic proof that Lp(a) causes cardiovascular disease, converting a long-neglected biomarker into a causal target now pursued by drug developers.

name: Borge G. Nordestgaard
region: University of Copenhagen / Copenhagen University Hospital, Denmark

primary_works.title: Lipoprotein(a) as a cardiovascular risk factor: current status - EAS consensus (Eur Heart J)
Copenhagen General Population Study Mendelian-randomization program

field_contribution: Architect of the Copenhagen cohort Mendelian-randomization program, which used large genetically-characterized population samples to test causality for Lp(a), remnant cholesterol, triglycerides, and other lipid biomarkers, establishing a reusable template for distinguishing causal lipid exposures from confounded correlations.
why_indexed: Built the population-genetics machinery behind much of modern causal lipid epidemiology; senior author across the Copenhagen causal-biomarker literature.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (Lp(a)/Copenhagen cohorts; Kamstrup co-author)

name: Robert Clarke
region: University of Oxford (Nuffield Department of Population Health / CTSU), UK

primary_works.title: Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease - PROCARDIS (NEJM)
Homocysteine and coronary heart disease meta-analyses

field_contribution: Co-led the PROCARDIS genetic study showing LPA variants that raise Lp(a) also raise coronary-disease risk - independent genetic corroboration of Lp(a) causality - and contributed to the homocysteine and lipid epidemiology literature on which biomarker-mortality claims rest.
why_indexed: Supplied independent large-scale genetic-variant evidence that Lp(a) level causally tracks coronary disease.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (Lp(a) PROCARDIS genetics, NEJM 2009)

name: Paul M. Ridker
region: Harvard Medical School / Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston, USA

primary_works.title: Rosuvastatin to prevent vascular events in men and women with elevated CRP - JUPITER (NEJM)
Antiinflammatory therapy with canakinumab for atherosclerotic disease - CANTOS (NEJM)

field_contribution: Championed high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) as a measurable index of vascular inflammation predicting cardiovascular events, ran JUPITER (a statin trial that enrolled on CRP rather than LDL) and CANTOS (which lowered events with an anti-inflammatory antibody at unchanged LDL), supplying trial evidence for the inflammation hypothesis of atherosclerosis.
why_indexed: The reference figure linking a measurable inflammatory biomarker (hsCRP) to cardiovascular risk and testing it in randomized trials - the empirical anchor of the residual-inflammatory-risk concept.
cross_branch_note: links to Domain B inflammaging (Franceschi) as a measurable vascular endpoint
disputed: The clinical primacy of CRP-guided therapy is debated; JUPITER's effect size and CRP's incremental value over standard risk factors have been contested.

name: John Danesh (Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration)

primary_works.title: C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and mortality - ERFC (Lancet)
Diabetes mellitus, fasting glucose, and risk of cause-specific death - ERFC (NEJM)

field_contribution: Leads the Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration, which pools individual-participant data from scores of prospective cohorts to estimate biomarker-mortality associations at a scale and rigor (adjustment, regression-dilution correction) unavailable to single studies - producing the highest-tier evidence on CRP, fibrinogen, glucose, and lipids as risk predictors.
why_indexed: The consortium and methodology behind the most authoritative biomarker-versus-mortality effect estimates; the standard against which single-cohort biomarker claims are checked.
disputed: Indexed as a consortium-anchored figure; ERFC findings often temper enthusiastic single-study biomarker claims by showing modest incremental predictive value.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (CRP, fasting-glucose IPD meta-analyses)

name: Elizabeth Selvin
region: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, Baltimore, USA

primary_works.title: Glycated hemoglobin, diabetes, and cardiovascular risk in nondiabetic adults - ARIC (NEJM)
Hemoglobin A1c and risk of mortality and cardiovascular disease - ARIC analyses

field_contribution: Showed in the ARIC cohort that glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) - a time-integrated measure of glycemia - predicts cardiovascular disease and death even within the non-diabetic range, helping move HbA1c from a diabetes-monitoring tool to a continuous risk biomarker.
why_indexed: Established HbA1c as a graded mortality/CVD predictor across the glycemic spectrum, the empirical basis for using it as a longevity-relevant metric in non-diabetics.

name: Stephanie A. Studenski
region: University of Pittsburgh, USA (formerly National Institute on Aging)

primary_works.title: Gait speed and survival in older adults (JAMA)
Physical performance measures in the clinical setting (J Am Geriatr Soc)

field_contribution: Pooled-analysis lead establishing that usual gait speed predicts survival in older adults about as well as multi-factor clinical models, turning a simple walking-speed measurement into a validated functional aging biomarker.
why_indexed: Made gait speed a credentialed survival predictor - the canonical example of a cheap functional metric rivaling complex panels.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (gait-speed survival pooled analysis)

name: Rachel Cooper & Diana Kuh
region: Cooper: Manchester Metropolitan University, UK (formerly MRC Unit for Lifelong Health & Ageing). Kuh: University College London (MRC LHA director)

primary_works.title: Objectively measured physical capability levels and mortality: systematic review and meta-analysis (BMJ)
Life-course determinants of physical capability (MRC LHA program)

field_contribution: Conducted the omnibus meta-analysis showing that grip strength, gait speed, chair-rise time, and standing-balance each independently predict all-cause mortality, establishing a panel of simple physical-capability measures as aging biomarkers within a life-course framework.
why_indexed: The single most cited synthesis demonstrating that multiple cheap functional tests - not just one - independently forecast mortality.
disputed: Indexed as a paired-author card (Cooper first author, Kuh senior author / program director).

name: Anne B. Newman
region: University of Pittsburgh (Center for Aging and Population Health), USA

primary_works.title: Strength and muscle quality in a well-functioning cohort - Health ABC (J Am Geriatr Soc)
Sarcopenia, muscle strength and mortality - Health ABC analyses

field_contribution: Showed in the Health ABC cohort that DXA-measured lean muscle mass does not independently predict mortality once muscle strength is accounted for, the empirical root of the field's shift from 'muscle mass' to 'muscle strength/function' as the protective variable.
why_indexed: Provided the data that reframed sarcopenia outcomes around strength rather than mass - a correction repeatedly cited against mass-centric body-composition claims.

name: Jennifer L. Kuk & Peter T. Katzmarzyk
region: Kuk: York University, Toronto, Canada. Katzmarzyk: Pennington Biomedical Research Center, Baton Rouge, USA

primary_works.title: Visceral fat is an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in men (Obesity)
Body fat distribution and mortality - imaging-cohort analyses

field_contribution: Showed using imaging-quantified adiposity that visceral adipose tissue independently predicts all-cause mortality beyond BMI and waist circumference, supporting fat distribution (where fat sits) over total fat mass as the metabolically relevant measurement.
why_indexed: The empirical basis for prioritizing visceral over total or subcutaneous fat as a mortality-relevant body-composition biomarker.
disputed: Indexed as a paired-author card (Kuk first author, with Katzmarzyk and Ross collaborators).

name: Robert Ross

primary_works.title: Importance of assessing cardiorespiratory fitness in clinical practice - AHA Scientific Statement (Circulation)
Reduction in obesity and related comorbid conditions after diet-induced weight loss or exercise (Ann Intern Med)

field_contribution: Led the American Heart Association statement arguing cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF/VO2max) should be measured as a routine clinical vital sign, and produced imaging-based work on exercise effects on visceral fat, joining the 'fitness as the strongest modifiable mortality predictor' argument to a measurement recommendation.
why_indexed: The figure who pushed cardiorespiratory fitness from a research variable toward a recommended clinical vital sign.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (AHA CRF-as-vital-sign statement; visceral-fat co-author)

name: Hisako Tsuji
region: Moriguchi City Health Examination Center, Japan / Framingham Heart Study collaboration

primary_works.title: Reduced heart rate variability and mortality risk in an elderly cohort - Framingham (Circulation)
Impact of reduced heart rate variability on risk for cardiac events - Framingham (Circulation)

field_contribution: First-authored the Framingham analyses linking reduced heart-rate variability (HRV) - a measure of autonomic/parasympathetic tone - to elevated mortality and cardiac-event risk in a community cohort, establishing HRV as a population-level prognostic biomarker.
why_indexed: The foundational cohort evidence that HRV predicts mortality, underpinning the now-ubiquitous use of HRV in wearables and recovery tracking.

name: Evan D. Chinoy
region: Naval Health Research Center, San Diego, USA (formerly Brigham and Women's Hospital)

primary_works.title: Performance of seven consumer sleep-tracking devices compared with polysomnography (Sleep)
Validation of consumer sleep-tracking technology (follow-up validations)

field_contribution: Ran head-to-head validations showing that consumer sleep-tracking devices estimate total sleep time reasonably but stage sleep (light/deep/REM) poorly against polysomnography, quantifying the gap between marketed and measured sleep metrics.
why_indexed: The reference validity check on consumer sleep wearables - the empirical caveat against over-trusting sleep-stage numbers from rings and watches.
surfaced_via: Wave: Domain L (consumer sleep-tracker vs PSG validation)

name: Boris Kovatchev
region: University of Virginia (Center for Diabetes Technology), Charlottesville, USA

primary_works.title: Comparison of the numerical and clinical accuracy of continuous glucose monitors
Metrics for glycemic control - variability and risk (control-variability grid)

field_contribution: Developed the accuracy metrics and variability/risk analytics for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and closed-loop ('artificial pancreas') systems, and showed that numerical and clinical accuracy differ across sensors - the measurement-quality foundation under any CGM-based metabolic claim.
why_indexed: The engineer behind how CGM accuracy is defined and compared - the validity layer beneath consumer/quantified-self glucose tracking.

name: Anthony J. Hanley

primary_works.title: Homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance in relation to incident cardiovascular disease - IRAS (Diabetes Care)
Insulin resistance and the metabolic syndrome - IRAS analyses

field_contribution: Showed in the Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Study (IRAS) that HOMA-IR, a fasting-insulin-and-glucose index of insulin resistance, predicts incident cardiovascular disease, supporting fasting insulin resistance as an early-warning metabolic biomarker before overt dysglycemia.
why_indexed: Provided cohort evidence that a simple fasting-derived insulin-resistance index forecasts cardiovascular disease, anchoring the 'measure insulin resistance early' argument.

name: Kay Ahn (Pfizer SIRT1 biochemistry group)

primary_works.title: SRT1720, SRT2183, SRT1460, and resveratrol are not direct activators of SIRT1 - Pacholec, Ahn et al. (J Biol Chem)

field_contribution: Reported, with colleagues at Pfizer (and separately Amgen), that the apparent SIRT1 'activation' by resveratrol and the Sirtris STAC compounds was a fluorophore-substrate assay artifact - activation appeared only with a non-physiological fluorogenic peptide and vanished with native substrate - supplying the empirical biochemical check on the resveratrol-longevity claims.
why_indexed: Indexed as the group behind the in-vitro result that directly contested the mechanism underlying a major longevity-supplement narrative - an example of an empirical refutation entering the canon's evidence layer.
disputed: The assay-artifact finding is itself contested; Sinclair and Sirtris/GSK argued allosteric activation is real with native substrates bearing hydrophobic residues. Indexed as a documented scientific disagreement, not a settled verdict. INCLUSION != ENDORSEMENT.

name: Leonardo Brito & Claudio Gil Araujo
region: CLINIMEX / Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

primary_works.title: Ability to sit and rise from the floor as a predictor of all-cause mortality (Eur J Prev Cardiol)

field_contribution: Developed and validated the sitting-rising test (SRT) - scoring how few supports a person needs to lower to and rise from the floor - and showed in a middle-aged-and-older cohort that lower SRT scores predict higher all-cause mortality, converting a musculoskeletal-fitness movement into a hard-outcome biomarker.
why_indexed: The outcome-anchored evidence beneath floor-mobility and 'sit-to-rise' advice; a rare case where a simple movement test is tied directly to mortality data.
disputed: Indexed as a paired-author card (Brito first author, Araujo senior author / CLINIMEX director).

name: Patanjali
lifespan: fl. c. 2nd c. BCE – 4th c. CE (disputed)

primary_works.title: Yoga Sutras of Patanjali (compiled)

field_contribution: Compiled the Yoga Sutras, the foundational text of classical yoga, codifying the 'eight limbs' (ashtanga): ethical restraints, posture (asana — described only as a 'steady, comfortable seat'), breath control (pranayama), sense-withdrawal, concentration, meditation (dhyana) and absorption (samadhi). The text is a meditative/philosophical system, NOT a manual of physical postures.
why_indexed: The textual/historical root invoked by nearly all modern yoga, and the source most often mis-cited to lend ancient authority to postural (asana) practice — a conflation the corpus keeps explicit. Cultural provenance, not biological evidence.
cross_branch_note: Bridges to the 07-mind branch (philosophy of consciousness/attention) as a historical contemplative-systems text.
disputed: Authorship/date and whether one or several 'Patanjali' authors are uncertain; routinely mis-cited as authority for physical-posture yoga.

name: T. Krishnamacharya

primary_works.title: Yoga Makaranda (book)
Mysore Palace teaching lineage

field_contribution: 'Father of modern yoga.' Fused medieval Hatha asana with gymnastic/physical-culture movement, breath-synchronized flow (vinyasa) and therapeutic individualization, then taught the students who exported yoga globally — Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, Desikachar, Indra Devi. Nearly every globally practiced postural style traces to his Mysore school.
why_indexed: The single lineage node from which the two most-studied modern styles (Iyengar, Ashtanga) descend — the historical root under almost all yoga-as-medicine research interventions.
surfaced_via: Wave 5 F2 yoga/meditation lineages (modern root; teacher of Iyengar & Jois)

name: K. Pattabhi Jois

primary_works.title: Yoga Mala (book)
Ashtanga Mysore method / fixed series

field_contribution: Systematized and popularized Ashtanga Vinyasa yoga: fixed, demanding sequences of postures linked breath-to-movement (vinyasa) with ujjayi breath, bandhas and drishti. The athletic, sweat-driven parent style of Western 'power yoga' and much of modern vinyasa flow.
why_indexed: Codifier of the most physically intense mainstream yoga lineage — relevant to cardiorespiratory/strength load and to higher injury exposure than gentle/restorative styles. Index the method separately from the man.
disputed: Index the method, not the man: later abuse allegations against Jois are a credibility flag on the person, not on the movement physiology.

name: Jon Kabat-Zinn

primary_works.title: MBSR program, UMass Stress Reduction Clinic
Full Catastrophe Living (book)
Davidson & Kabat-Zinn et al., Alterations in brain and immune function produced by mindfulness meditation (Psychosom Med)

field_contribution: Created Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) in 1979 — an 8-week secularized clinical program (body scan, sitting meditation, gentle Hatha yoga) that stripped meditation of religious framing so it could enter medicine and be studied in RCTs. The single intervention that made 'mindfulness' a research and clinical object; parent of MBCT and the broader mindfulness movement.
why_indexed: MBSR is the most-studied meditation intervention; it anchors the meditation evidence base (Davidson 2003 immune/brain study; the Goyal 2014 meta is largely MBSR/MBCT trials). Honest read: moderate evidence for anxiety/depression/pain, weak for most else, expectancy-/active-control-limited.
cross_branch_note: Bridges to 07-mind (attention/consciousness) as the secular clinical translation of contemplative practice.

name: Herbert Benson

primary_works.title: Wallace, Benson & Wilson, A wakeful hypometabolic physiologic state (Am J Physiol)
The Relaxation Response (book)

field_contribution: Showed physiologically that meditation (initially TM) elicits a reproducible 'relaxation response' — reduced oxygen consumption, heart rate, respiratory rate and sympathetic arousal ('a wakeful hypometabolic state'). Then de-religioned it into a generic technique (a repeated word/phrase + passive attitude), arguing the physiology is tradition-independent. Founder of Harvard's Mind/Body Medical Institute.
why_indexed: Provides the mechanism layer beneath 'meditation relaxes you' — a measurable autonomic/metabolic shift — and the bridge between TM (a commercialized lineage) and secular clinical practice. A mechanism finding, NOT an outcome: relaxation physiology is not disease or longevity benefit.
disputed: Early TM-based work shares the TM-research allegiance-bias concern (see conflict-tm-research-allegiance-bias); the generic relaxation-response physiology is the durable, non-TM-specific part.

name: Richard J. Davidson

primary_works.title: Davidson & Kabat-Zinn et al., Alterations in brain and immune function produced by mindfulness meditation (Psychosom Med)
Lutz et al., Long-term meditators self-induce high-amplitude gamma synchrony (PNAS)

field_contribution: Founder of contemplative neuroscience — the rigorous neuroscience of meditation. Showed an 8-week MBSR course shifted prefrontal EEG asymmetry toward a positive-affect pattern AND improved antibody response to influenza vaccine (2003), and that long-term Tibetan adepts can self-generate high-amplitude gamma EEG synchrony (2004). Founded the Center for Healthy Minds.
why_indexed: The lab that converted meditation from anecdote into a brain/immune measurement program — the credible end of the contemplative-science literature. Caveat: his foundational studies are small (n in the tens) and the field's wider claims (telomeres, longevity) far outrun this rigorous core.
